name: AFP
label: AFP
why: AFP's own wire on france24.com/en/live-news (credited AFP): one-line informative headlines ('All contenders for UN chief receive veto: diplomat'), ~100 a day, often first. The radar has no AFP today; France 24's Middle East feed is a different, slower desk. Some sport in it (the noise filter takes most).
link_note: article pages refuse plain scripted clients (HTTP 403); a normal web fetch opened the article with its AFP credit on 2026-10-17

name: Reuters seneste time
label: Reuters
why: Companion to the existing 'Reuters' entry, not a replacement: Google News returns at most 100 items per query and Reuters publishes far more a day, so 'when:1d' misses most fresh items (of the last hour's 7 only 2 were in the 1-day result). A 1-hour window polled every 5 minutes catches nearly all; same links, so the radar's dedupe merges them, and 'outlet: Reuters' keeps it one outlet.

name: AP seneste time
label: AP
why: Same as Reuters: of AP's last-hour items only half were in the 1-day top 100. Companion to 'AP' (outlet AP); AP's own RSS sits behind a Cloudflare challenge.

name: العربية
label: Al Arabiya
why: Al Arabiya's own verified Telegram channel (114K, links alarabiya.net): wire-style Arabic lines ('Putin's envoy: Russia and America will soon announce new joint initiatives'), ~80 a day. The Saudi camp's counterpart to Al Jazeera's ajanews wire; Al Arabiya's websites answer 403 to the radar. Al Hadath's channel carries the same lines, so only one of the two.

name: Axios
why: Short informative headlines and frequent firsts on the leading state's decisions and its Middle East diplomacy (Barak Ravid: 'Iran-backed militias sending money back to cash-starved IRGC, U.S. says'); ~15 a day.
link_note: article pages refuse non-browser clients (HTTP 403); opened fine in a browser on 2026-10-17

name: QNA
label: Qatar News Agency
why: Qatar's state agency, its 'Qatar' feed: the Amir's, the PM/foreign minister's and the ministries' acts ('Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs Affirms Qatar's Continued Support for Lebanon'), ~15 a day. The Qatari camp has Al Jazeera but no state voice.

name: WAM
label: WAM (Emiraterne)
why: The UAE's state agency (its own site has no feed). Noisy (~60 a day, festivals and ceremonies), but the only Emirati official voice; as an official source it never leads a story and adds at most a few cards.

name: SIS Egypt
label: Egyptens statsinformationstjeneste
why: Egypt's State Information Service (under the presidency): the regime's own wording ('Egypt, Sudan FMs reject attempts to undermine bilateral ties'), ~12 a day. MENA's own feed does not parse and the presidency's is broken. '-Masar -Ministan' keeps out SIS's Hausa-language copies.

name: Petra
label: Petra (Jordan)
why: Jordan's state agency (new camp jo): the King's and government's positions ('Jordan Welcomes UN Security Council Condemnation of Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia'), ~13 a day. Some titles keep a ' - The Jordan News Agency' tail.

name: INA
label: Iraqi News Agency
why: Iraq's state agency (Shafaq is the camp's only source): ~25 a day. Its own RSS stopped in May 2026. Many titles end in '» Iraqi News Agency' (the radar strips only ' - …'), hence the lower fit.

name: سانا
label: SANA
why: Syria's state agency, its verified channel linked from sana.sy (133K): the new government's acts and ministers' statements, ~80 a day. The English RSS stopped on 29 Sep and the Arabic one does not parse. Enab Baladi is the camp's only source today.

name: Saba
label: Saba (Yemens regering)
why: The recognised Yemeni government's agency (sabanew.net, not the Houthi-run saba.ye): ~6 English items a day ('Yemen Welcomes UN Security Council Presidential Statement on Houthi Attacks Against Yemen, Saudi Arabia'). New camp ye while the Houthi-Saudi war is a lead story.

name: ONA
label: Oman News Agency
why: Oman's state agency (new camp om), the mediator between Washington and Tehran; English feed, uneven pace (55 items in 3 days). Arabic politics feed rss.ona?cat=5 is the alternative.

name: APS
label: Algérie Presse Service
why: Algeria's state agency (new camp dz): President Tebboune's acts and the state line on Morocco and France, ~25 a day with some culture and trade fairs. Its own site has no feed.

name: Bernama
why: Malaysia's state agency (new camp my). Low priority: ~85 a day, mostly domestic. Google News gives clean, dated titles; Bernama's own RSS has no dates and 'General :' prefixes.

name: UK Prime Minister
label: Storbritanniens premierminister
why: Number 10's own feed: the PM's calls, meetings and statements ('PM meeting with President Zelenskyy of Ukraine'), ~1-2 a day, half domestic. A great power's head of government; the FCDO is followed, Downing Street is not.

name: US Treasury
label: USA's finansministerium
why: The leading state's sanctions as they are issued ('Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran's International Financial Networks and Shadow Banking Architecture'), 1-2 a day. Treasury/OFAC's own feeds are gone or blocked; old Treasury pages in the result are dropped by the radar's age limit.

name: US Department of War
label: Pentagon
why: The Pentagon's releases feed (renamed Department of War): readouts and decisions ('Readout of Secretary of War Pete Hegseth's Meeting With the United Kingdom's Secretary of State for Defence'), ~5 a week. war.gov runs bot protection; if GitHub's runners get 403, the caretaker should disable it (Google News for war.gov is mostly junk).
link_note: article pages refuse non-browser clients (HTTP 403); opened fine in a browser on 2026-10-17

name: US Mission to the UN
label: USA's FN-mission
why: The leading state's words in the Security Council, ~1 a day. Titles say only where ('Remarks at a UN Security Council Briefing on the Situation in the Middle East'); the teaser carries what was said.

name: France MFA
label: Frankrigs udenrigsministerium
why: A great power's foreign ministry ('Iran – Summoning of the Islamic Republic of Iran's chargé d'affaires in France'), ~5 a day; the ministry's own RSS answers 403. Noisy: embassy pages and search pages come along.

name: China MFA
label: Kinas udenrigsministerium
why: Beijing's own record of Wang Yi's talks and statements ('Wang Yi Meets with Palestinian Foreign Minister'), ~5 a day. Some titles end in '_Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the People's Republic of China'; the spokesperson's press-conference titles name no content.

name: Turkey MFA
label: Tyrkiets udenrigsministerium
why: Ankara's numbered statements ('No: 199, 16 October 2026, Regarding Appointments to Vacant Ministerial Positions in the Iraqi Cabinet', joint statements of the Muslim countries' foreign ministers), 1-3 a day. Feed holds its whole archive (166 KB).

name: Turkey MFA minister
label: Tyrkiets udenrigsministerium
why: Hakan Fidan's meetings, who with and where ('Minister of Foreign Affairs Hakan Fidan met with Halil el-Hayya, Chief of Hamas Political Bureau, 9 October 2026, Ankara'), ~1 a day; same outlet as the statements.

name: رئاسة الجمهورية العربية السورية
label: Syriens præsidentembede
why: The Syrian presidency's verified channel (184K): al-Sharaa's meetings, calls and agreements, a few a week.

name: OIC
label: Den Islamiske Samarbejdsorganisation (OIC)
why: The Muslim world's rulers as a bloc (the foreign ministers' council in Baghdad these days), ~1 a day.

name: GCC Secretariat
label: Golfstaternes Samarbejdsråd (GCC)
why: The Gulf rulers' joint statements ('Statement Issued by the GCC General Secretariat Regarding the Rescheduling of the GCC-EU Summit'), ~3 a day.

name: Statsministeriet
why: The Prime Minister's own press releases ('Aftale mellem Grønland, Danmark og USA', 'Udtalelse fra statsminister Mette Frederiksen'), ~3 a month and each one matters. Caveat: the feed is the whole archive, ~1 MB per fetch (no paging, no gzip), and dates are midnight UTC.

name: Udenrigsministeriet
why: The foreign ministry's press releases through Via Ritzau (um.dk's news page is this list): Danish foreign policy first-hand ('Danmark og Brasilien indgår strategisk partnerskab'), ~3 a week.

name: Udlændinge- og Integrationsministeriet
why: The ministry for the group's core Danish subject, first-hand ('Regeringen vil indføre screeningsmodel for ansøgere til dansk statsborgerskab', 'Bødskov: Ekstrem islamisme og æresrelateret vold …'), ~2 a week. Its Via Ritzau feed stopped in 2025; this is the site's own list.

name: Justitsministeriet
why: Justice ministry releases (PET, border control, laws touching religion such as the Quran-burning law), ~2 a week; some animal-welfare and flag-day items.

name: Naharnet
why: Lebanon (new camp lb) with wire-like headlines ('Rubio tells Aoun not to return seized explosives to Hezbollah', 'Qatari PM meets Aoun, says Israel must let Lebanese Army deploy in South'), ~25 a day. Naharnet's own RSS and L'Orient Today's feeds do not parse; the state agency NNA has no feed.

name: Rudaw
why: The Kurdistan Region's view (new camp krd) on Iraq, Iran, Syria and Turkey ('Iraq estimates losses from US-Iran war at $60 billion'), ~12 a day. Its own RSS does not parse.

name: Kyiv Independent
why: Ukraine's side of the war in Europe (new camp ua), informative headlines ('US lawmaker introduces bill blocking Trump's Russian diesel deal'), ~15 a day. Preferred over the state agency Ukrinform (more domestic trivia).

name: Libya Herald
why: Libya (new camp ly): central bank, oil revenue and the rival governments, ~7 a day.

name: Dabanga
why: Sudan's war (new camp sd) from an independent Sudanese newsroom ('UN and Switzerland plan Sudan peace talks as US lawmaker proposes resource partnership'), ~2 a day. Sudan Tribune and the state agency SUNA answer 403.

name: Yonhap
why: Low priority: the Far East issue has only Chinese state sources. Korea's wire, plain headlines ('N. Korea conducts underwater test of new precision-guided torpedo'), but ~70 a day, mostly Korean domestic.
